slides.title: Cues: the shortcut layer for real life
slides.purpose: From a location arrival to a family check-in, Cues turns a human sentence into a reviewable, secure mobile workflow.

slides.title: People remember outcomes, not taps
slides.purpose: Reaching the office, buying vegetables, following up a missed call, and studying from daily mail are repeated intent—not separate apps and manual checklists.

slides.title: The hero flow: arrive at Office → family knows
slides.purpose: A declared 150 m Office place detects an arrival; Cues applies an at-most-once-per-local-day guard, then opens WhatsApp with “I am in office” addressed to Wish. The human still chooses the chat and taps Send.

slides.title: A shortcut you can inspect before it exists
slides.purpose: The cue is parsed into WHEN: arrive at Office; DO: WhatsApp draft for Wish; REPEAT: once per local day. Permissions, forecast, and effects are visible before arming.

slides.title: Context turns requests into timely help
slides.purpose: “Buy 2 kg potato and 2 kg tomato” becomes a reviewable task with a notification, WhatsApp draft, and Gmail handoff—only when the user chooses the relevant place, time, or shopping context.

slides.title: Missed call → respectful follow-up
slides.purpose: A future call-state adapter can detect a missed call, wait for a user-defined quiet period, then notify, create a callback task, or prepare—not send—a reply. The player loop makes timing and reversal visible.

slides.title: Daily mail becomes a learning ritual
slides.purpose: When a daily study email is read, choose one outcome: Sarvam voice note to yourself in WhatsApp, a concise attention summary, or Gemma-generated MCQs in a parsable review format.

slides.title: Choice of model, one deterministic safety boundary
slides.purpose: Download and verify an on-device Gemma model for private drafting; optionally use Sarvam for selected-language speech and translation. Neither model executes an action or grants itself a capability.

slides.title: Speak and write in the language you chose
slides.purpose: Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Telugu, and Tamil remain visible in their own script. Sarvam receives the explicit language code; only a private submitted copy is normalized for the existing parser.

slides.title: The next shortcut is a sentence away
slides.purpose: Choose a workflow: office check-in, grocery reminder, missed-call follow-up, email-to-MCQ, or recurring alarm. Cues keeps it local-first, reviewable, and honest about what still needs the user’s final tap.
slides.constraints: Local-first by default; cloud language assistance is opt-in; personal WhatsApp always ends with a visible user Send tap; every automation is explicitly approved.
